body_markdown:
Ford gave[the Jeep Wrangler](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/review-2022-jeep-wrangler-rubicon-392/) its first direct rival in many years when it resurrected[the Bronco](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-ford-bronco-stroppe-review-dapper-wrapper/) for the 2021 model year. According to a new report, the brand now has its sights set on[the Gladiator truck](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2026-jeep-gladiator-sahara-pictures-specs-pricing/) , which claims a Ford Bronco pickup is due out in the coming years.


According to the industry trade journal *[Automotive News](https://www.autonews.com/car-concepts/future-product/an-ford-future-product-0819/)* , the move is part of Ford’s effort to turn its most popular vehicles into sub-brands. This same strategy will spawn[the first four-door Mustang](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/four-door-ford-mustang-rumors-price-launch-date/) in the not-too-distant future, according to a separate report.


Anonymous sources familiar with Ford’s product pipeline told the publication that the Bronco pickup will make its debut by the end of the decade. There’s no word yet on whether it will land as a two-door truck or if it will offer four doors, though we’d bet that the latter configuration is more likely. And, we expect that a Bronco truck would be positioned in the same space as the Gladiator, meaning it will put a much bigger focus on adventure, customization, and off-road capability than on towing capacity and payload.


Ford is developing a play truck, then, which makes sense: It already offers a wide selection of pickups ranging from[the Maverick](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-ford-maverick-lobo-review-street-truck-reborn/) to[the F-Series Super Duty](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-ford-super-duty-carhartt-package-is-a-tasteful-nod-to-workwear/) , and is churning out more, including the new[Fathom EV](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/getting-to-the-bottom-of-fords-28350-fathom/) . It will need to position the Bronco pickup carefully to ensure it doesn’t overlap with other trucks.

It’s not far-fetched to speculate that the Bronco pickup will offer the same off-road goodies as the SUV, such as the G.O.A.T. modes, electronic-locking front and rear differentials, and Trail Turn Assist. We’d love to see a[Bronco Raptor](https://www.hagerty.com/media/video/fords-bronco-raptor-can-beat-your-muscle-car-in-the-quarter-mile-just-add-dirt/) pickup, too.


Ford would likely build the Bronco pickup alongside the SUV model in its Michigan Assembly Plant, according to the same report. The plant will also make a Lincoln-based Bronco starting in 2029, while production of the next-generation Ranger will reportedly move to Tennessee. Interestingly, the company could ditch the Ranger nameplate in the United States, *Automotive News* wrote.


Ford would not confirm the report’s assertions. “We are not going to comment on future product speculation, much of which is inaccurate. What we can say is Ford is focused on delivering a massive product renewal that will refresh 80% of our North American portfolio by volume by 2029. This includes the all-new[Ford Fathom](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/getting-to-the-bottom-of-fords-28350-fathom/) midsize pickup on the new Universal Electric Vehicle platform, alongside the next-generation F-150 and F-Series Super Duty,” a spokesperson told *Hagerty* .


If the report is accurate, we’ll learn more about the Ford Bronco pickup in the coming months.


The post[Report: Ford Bronco Pickup Could Step into the Gladiator Arena](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-bronco-pickup-launch-date-report/) appeared first on[Hagerty Media](https://www.hagerty.com/media) .
